neighbours.label: the copula (is/are/was) after a fronted predicate phrase, with the subject following it (inversion: 'New to the menu is X', 'Rounding out the list are Y')
fire: Also new at the library this autumn is a corner for teenage readers.
Joining the band on stage tonight are two violinists from Lisbon.
What is less well known, however, is that the castle once had a moat.
Rounding out the shortlist are three novels by first-time authors.
New to the gallery this season is a room of early Dutch landscapes.
Among the guests at the opening dinner were the mayor and her husband.
What became clear during the trial, though, was that the records were missing.
Included in the ticket price are a guided tour and a cup of coffee.
quiet: The library opened a corner for teenage readers this autumn.
Two violinists from Lisbon will join the band on stage tonight.
Few people know, however, that the castle once had a moat.
Three novels by first-time authors complete the shortlist.
The gallery added a room of early Dutch landscapes this season.
The mayor and her husband attended the opening dinner as guests.
During the trial it became clear, though, that the records were missing.
The ticket price covers a guided tour and a cup of coffee.

notes: Card + pole: ' is' x18 in inversions ('In attendance ... was Rob Lewis', 'Rounding out Curiosity's cameras are', 'What is less evident, though, is', 'New to the site this month is'); - pole is 'which are'. Probe: 'What is less obvious, though, is' 0.65, 'New to the menu this month is' 0.57, 'Rounding out the lineup are' 0.47, 'In attendance ... was' 0.27; canonical rewrites 0.02-0.04, 'which are' 0.02, short 'Most important of all is' 0.01 (so the fronted phrase needs some length). Near misses keep content in canonical order.
